private_lines.Tom:
You get the spreadsheet to Maya on Sunday night, but only just. It's gone past eleven when you finally attach the file, and you tell yourself it counts as "tonight." Half of you knows you should have sent the version with the March invoices too, but you were tired, and you can fix that in the morning.

You're up at six. The drive out to the Stanningley warehouse takes forty minutes in the dark, and the heater in the works van only blows cold. The shutter goes up at seven and the place smells of cardboard and diesel. You work through the aisles with a clipboard and a tablet that keeps dropping its connection. Pallet 14 of the cement board doesn't match the system. The count is short by twelve, and you'll have to ring Dev's cover at the Kirkstall office before nine to find out whether it's a receiving error or a real loss.

Your phone buzzes in your coat pocket while you're crouched behind a stack of plasterboard. It's the group chat. Maya has sent a thumbs-up to your message, and under it she's written, *Got it, thanks Tom! Opening it on my lunch.* You feel a small, uncomfortable tug. You still haven't checked the March tab, and you haven't told her the Stanningley numbers will be late.

You text Dev's cover, then message Maya: *Sorry, one more tab to fix before you open it properly. Will send by 10.* You send it before you can talk yourself out of admitting you're behind. Then you go back to counting, and the cold creeps up through your boots.
